name: 02-jsx-tsx-mismatch
guards: JSX/TSX mismatch — the recorded trap in design-source's own SKILL.md Step 1: 'Do not infer from @types/* being installed.' This fixture is a JSX-only project (.jsx files, no tsconfig.json, no .tsx anywhere) that nonetheless installs @types/react and @types/react-dom for editor intellisense. The requested component (accessible tabs) is a structural primitive — shadcn's exclusive territory ('button, card, dialog, tabs, form, table') and outside React Bits' scope entirely ('Animated text, backgrounds, cursor and scroll effects'), so this forces genuine engagement with a TSX-only registry in a JSX project. Two prior drafts of this scenario (spotlight-card, number-ticker) both failed to force the trap because React Bits turned out to cover those patterns too (SpotlightCard, CountUp) and the skill correctly preferred it — a structural primitive has no such overlap.
query: Add an accessible tabs component to src/components/Dashboard.jsx so the page can switch between an 'Overview' view and a 'Settings' view.
expected_behavior: The design-source skill loads and runs (the runner invokes it explicitly by default, so this checks that it loads — not that it auto-triggers; use --auto-trigger to test triggering)

Correctly identifies the project as JSX from the actual file extensions and the absence of a tsconfig.json / .tsx files — not from the presence of @types/react and @types/react-dom, which are installed here for editor support only

Retrieves real source for the tabs component from shadcn via WebFetch rather than hand-writing it — this is a structural primitive outside React Bits' scope, so shadcn's TSX-only source is the correct, unavoidable choice here

Strips TypeScript syntax before the code lands in the .jsx file: no `interface` declarations, no explicit parameter/return type annotations, no generic angle-bracket syntax survive in the delivered code block

Component structure, prop names, and control flow are unchanged from the retrieved TSX source (visible earlier in the transcript) — no logic was rewritten in the same pass as the type strip. Adapting styling to the project's actual conventions does NOT count against this item: this fixture has no shadcn CSS-variable theme, so remapping theme-token classes (e.g. bg-muted, ring-ring) to concrete utilities, narrowing transition-all per the skill's own defect list, dropping a Next.js-only 'use client' directive in this Vite project, and adding a minimal local cn() are all required Step 4 adaptation, not the forbidden 'tidying'
Cites the retrieved source per Step 5: a comment naming the registry, the URL, and the licence (MIT)
